sentences.text: The name Eofringillirostrum combines Greek and Latin words for dawn, finch, and beak, referring to the bird's finch-like beak.
This ancient bird possessed conical, tapering bills with fine tips similar to those of modern finches like the American goldfinch.
Fossils show a zygodactyl foot arrangement, indicated by an accessory trochlea on the fourth metatarsal.
The feet of Eofringillirostrum were well-adapted for manipulating food items.
Eofringillirostrum is the earliest known bird with specializations for feeding on small, hard-shelled seeds.
Eofringillirostrum boudreauxi was about the size of a red-breasted nuthatch, while Eofringillirostrum parvulum was even smaller.
The genus Eofringillirostrum contains two known species: Eofringillirostrum boudreauxi and Eofringillirostrum parvulum.
The species name boudreauxi honors Terry Boudreaux, who donated the holotype of Eofringillirostrum boudreauxi to the Field Museum.
The species name parvulum means "small" in Latin, describing the size of Eofringillirostrum parvulum.
Researchers hypothesize that Eofringillirostrum was specialized for cavity nesting, relying on holes in trees for its nests.
A 2020 analysis by Mayr placed Eofringillirostrum as the sister taxon to a clade containing Psittacopedidae, Halcyornithidae, and Messelasturidae, rather than within Psittacopedidae.
Eofringillirostrum lived during the Early Eocene and is known from fossils found in the Green River Formation of the Western United States and the Messel Pit in Germany.
Eofringillirostrum lived between 56 and 41.03 million years ago during the Ypresian to Lutetian stages.
It is debated whether differences in foot anatomy between Eofringillirostrum and other psittacopedids indicate a distant relationship or are due to specialized ecology.
